key_insight: SqDRIFT-AIMD combines sampling-based quantum diagonalization with analytical nuclear gradients to extend quantum-centric molecular dynamics beyond active spaces tractable by exact diagonalization.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a path toward accurate electronic energies and nuclear forces for larger molecular simulations using quantum hardware.
method: Use randomized sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SqDRIFT).
Combine electronic-structure calculations with analytical nuclear gradients for AIMD.
Run quantum circuits on IBM Heron r3 processors to study proton transfer in the Zundel cation.
evidence_signal: At 40 qubits, SqDRIFT energies fall below CCSD across the double-well potential, while its AIMD trajectory tracks SHCI-driven proton transfer within 1.33 mÅ and conserves total energy with a standard deviation of 0.245 mE_h; at 52 qubits, energies remain within a few mE_h of CCSD.
watch_item: The reported molecular-dynamics validation is at 40 qubits; the 52-qubit energy results alone do not establish comparable trajectory accuracy or broader scalability.
paper_title: Towards large-scale ab initio Molecular Dynamics Simulation with Efficient Sampling-based Quantum Computing Algorithms
